57/S0.subgoal: Explain the focus of the lecture and the role of the 3D graphics pipeline in VR resource optimization.

57/S1.subgoal: Describe the basic idea of view transformation by comparing it to capturing a photograph.

57/S2.subgoal: List and describe the components and sequence of the viewing pipeline (view transformation, projection, window-to-viewport, clipping, and hidden surface removal).

57/S3.subgoal: Explain how the 3D viewing transformation sets up the view coordinate system using camera parameters.

57/S4.subgoal: Compare perspective projection and parallel projection and describe the required view volumes (frustum and parallelepiped) for each.

57/S5.subgoal: Explain the concept of a canonical view volume and how it is used to simplify pipeline computations.

57/S6.subgoal: Describe how projection is executed using specific transformation matrices for parallel and perspective methods.

57/S7.subgoal: Enumerate the complete sequence of transformations required to project a point from world coordinates to the 2D view plane.

57/S8.subgoal: Explain the window-to-viewport transformation used to map projected points onto the final display device space.

57/S9.subgoal: Describe the processes of clipping and hidden surface removal, and explain how they reduce computational complexity.

57/S10.subgoal: Summarize the stages of the graphics pipeline and the implications of knowledge gained regarding resource optimization.
